lastText: File ClosedOne Doctrine, No Second ChairContestedThe Joint Chiefs of Staff, 1940–1945A fleet that fights its entire final year, Iwo Jima, Okinawa, and whatever Downfall or blockade follows, under a single, consistent doctrine rather than alternating between two commanders' really different instincts. Spruance's caution costs the aggressive pursuit Halsey's style occasionally bought, and buys a fleet that never again sails into a typhoon it should have seen coming. The rest of the war's actual shape, the islands still to be taken, the war's actual conclusion still to be decided, unfolds on nearly the same calendar regardless of which admiral's temperament was running the fast carriers.The Theater Map at the end of the warPacific Situation · The war as it ended · Theater MapJapan: Contested (tap for why)Formosa: Contested (tap for why)Manchukuo: ContestedNorth China: ContestedEast China: ContestedGuangdong: ContestedHunan-Guangxi: Allied-controlled / liberatedFree China: Allied-controlled / liberatedYan'an: Allied-controlled / liberatedTibet & Xinjiang: Neutral / not yet contestedIndochina: ContestedThailand: ContestedBurma: Allied-controlled / liberatedIndia: Allied-controlled / liberatedMalaya: ContestedSumatra: ContestedJava: ContestedBorneo: ContestedCelebes: ContestedMoluccas & Timor: ContestedLuzon: Contested (tap for why)Visayas: Contested (tap for why)Mindanao: Contested (tap for why)New Guinea: Allied-controlled / liberatedSolomons: Allied-controlled / liberatedAustral
